name: NCSSM Online
description: A collection of virtual learning opportunities from NCSSM, including full courses and enrichment experiences like math circles and inquiry-based academic exploration offered during the school year.

name: NCSSM Connect
description: Real-time, instructor-led NCSSM courses delivered through partner high schools, often provided at no cost to enrolled students.

name: Chapel Hill Math Circle
description: A collaborative math enrichment program where students tackle advanced concepts and challenging problems in a group setting, typically meeting twice each month.

name: Durham Tech Dual Enrollment
description: College-level coursework options that allow qualified high school students to earn college credit while completing their high school education, with eligibility requirements depending on the pathway.

name: Wake Tech Dual Enrollment
description: A tuition-free program that enables eligible high school students to earn college credits or workforce credentials, often counting toward both high school graduation and future college goals.

name: Future Teachers of NC
description: The Future Teachers of North Carolina (FTNC) program is designed to inspire high school juniors and seniors to explore a career in teaching by offering an engaging and rigorous experience that introduces them to the training, responsibilities, and real-world aspects of becoming an educator.

name: The Engineering Place
description: The Engineering Place aims to motivate future problem solvers, innovators, and engineers by offering strong engineering education programs for K–12 students. By delivering interactive, hands-on learning opportunities for students and meaningful professional development for educators, the organization works to make engineering engaging and accessible to learners of all backgrounds.

name: Health and Environment Scholars @Duke
description: Duke University’s Nicholas School of the Environment and School of Medicine partner with Durham Public Schools to offer a year-long Health and Environmental Scholars Program for talented, underserved high school students. The program includes weekly in-person sessions with guest speakers, along with weekend field trips and hands-on lab experiences.

name: Raleigh Little Theatre - Teens on State/Teens Backstage
description: The Teens on Stage / Teens Backstage program strengthens students’ theatre skills by linking classes with hands-on production work and real-world themes. Open to students with varied experience levels, the program also builds communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills that extend beyond the arts.

name: NC YMCA Youth & Government
description: Youth and Government is a national civic program that helps high school students develop leadership skills by engaging directly with the policymaking process. Through local school or YMCA delegations, students gain hands-on experience in government and learn how to create positive change in their communities.

name: Raleigh Youth Council
description: The Raleigh Youth Council gives high school students a voice in local issues while building leadership skills through civic engagement, service, and special youth conferences.

name: Raleigh Teen Connect (RTC)
description: Raleigh Teen Connect (RTC) is a free program that connects teens to City of Raleigh resources, programs, facilities, and community services.

name: NC-MSEN Pre-College Program
description: The NC State NC-MSEN Pre-College Program is a STEM enrichment initiative for students in grades 6–12 that prepares participants for college pathways in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics through academic and enrichment experiences.

name: NCDOT High School Internship Program
description: The NCDOT High School Internship Program offers students a paid, part-time internship with the North Carolina Department of Transportation, allowing them to gain hands-on experience over one or more semesters throughout the year.

name: Durham Sports Commission: HS Internship
description: This internship with the Durham Sports Commission gives students hands-on experience planning and running major sporting events, including tournaments and youth leagues. Interns work with staff on marketing, logistics, and community outreach while learning about sponsorships, scheduling, and on-site operations, gaining valuable experience in sports and business administration.

name: Red Hat HS Internship
description: Red Hat’s two-week tech internship offers students hands-on experience working on real projects in areas such as software development, IT infrastructure, and tech marketing under the mentorship of Red Hat engineers. Participants may code, contribute to open-source projects, and attend campus tours and career-focused seminars to explore life at a technology company.

name: Durham Youth Employed & Succeeding (YES)
description: Durham YES is a youth service program under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act that helps ages 16–24 prepare for education and employment.

name: Durham Literacy Center - College and Career Readiness Program
description: The Durham Literacy Center’s College and Career Readiness program supports students as they pursue jobs, further training, or college opportunities by providing the skills, knowledge, and guidance needed to advance in their careers or education.

name: Durham Literacy Center - Youth Achievement Program
description: The Durham Literacy Center’s Youth Achievement Program (YAP) offers free, individualized high school equivalency instruction for out-of-school young adults ages 16–24 in a supportive and structured environment. The program provides academic teaching, career and social skills counseling, positive role models, and exploration of postsecondary and career pathways, meeting Monday through Thursday at the Durham Literacy Center’s headquarters.

name: Health Careers Day On “The Hill”
description: Health Careers Day on the Hill introduces students to a range of healthcare professions through presentations from representatives of UNC’s health professional schools and the Duke Physician Assistant Program. The event also features hands-on workshops, such as Stop the Bleed training, and provides opportunities to connect with healthcare professionals while learning about college and career pathways in the health field.

name: Fusion Academy Chapel Hill
description: Fusion Academy Chapel Hill offers a personalized one-to-one learning model designed for middle and high school students who benefit from individualized academic support. Students work closely with teachers in one-on-one classes, participate in small group sessions, and engage in guided digital learning, all within a flexible schedule that provides daily feedback and accommodates different learning needs.

name: North Carolina Health Careers Initiative (NC-HCAP): HCIE Workshops
description: The HCIE Workshop Series offers interactive, hands-on sessions designed to spark interest in healthcare careers for students in grades 5–12. Through small group discussions and cooperative activities, participants explore health career pathways, build academic and goal-setting skills, and learn about college preparation and financial aid while developing their own career plans.

name: Raleigh Teen Connect Co-Op at Saint Monica Teen Center
description: The Raleigh Teen Connect Co-Op at Saint Monica Teen Center is a collaborative space designed to create a welcoming and supportive environment where teens can learn, grow, and build connections with one another. This shared space allows nonprofit organizations and teen-led groups to host a variety of programs, including educational and career-focused workshops, recreational activities, and creative projects.

name: Living Life as an Art
description: Living Life as an Art is a program for high school students that blends creativity, community, and personal growth to connect work and play in meaningful ways. Participants will create art, explore design, engage in hands-on activities, go on field trips, and take part in volunteer projects. The program focuses on helping teens discover themselves, build new skills, and make a positive impact—all while having fun. If you’re looking to better understand yourself, connect with your community, and grow alongside others, apply now and join the first meeting on October 15, 2025.

name: Wake Early College of Health and Science
description: This five year program, in partnership with WakeMed, allows students to earn a high school diploma while working toward an associate degree. Students complete two years of rigorous honors courses at the Perry Health Sciences Campus before finishing their remaining classes at the Scott Northern Wake Campus.

name: Wake Early College of Information and Biotechnologies
description: Located in the Lilly Science and Technology Center on the RTP Campus, this program allows students to earn a high school diploma while working toward an associate degree. It focuses on three areas: biotechnology, computer programming, and cybersecurity.

name: Vernon Malone College and Career Academy
description: Students meet high school graduation requirements while earning college credits that can be applied toward an associate degree, diploma, or certificate at Wake Tech.

name: North Wake College and Career Academy
description: Students fulfill high school graduation requirements while earning college credits that count toward an associate degree, diploma, or certificate at Wake Tech.

name: YMCA High School Leaders Club
description: Leaders Club is a year long leadership development program for middle and high school teens that offers hands on training and volunteer opportunities supporting YMCA programs and services. Along with building leadership through service, advisors introduce teens to the Y’s impact on the community and help prepare them to become future leaders.

name: YMCA Lightner Y Achievers
description: Clarence E. Lightner Y Achievers supports young people in exploring higher education and career goals by building the skills they need to succeed and serve as community role models. The program empowers students in grades 6 to 12 by connecting them with dedicated adult mentors who guide them on their path beyond high school.

name: YMCA Southeast Raleigh Fellowship
description: The Southeast Raleigh YMCA Teen and Young Adult Fellowship is a 24 week immersive program that empowers up to 30 young leaders to explore career paths, build leadership skills, and connect their sense of purpose to meaningful impact at no cost.

name: SKEMA Business School
description: SKEMA Business School offers immersive Summer School programs designed for students and young professionals seeking a global learning experience. These short term programs combine academic rigor, cultural exploration, and real world business insights while emphasizing innovation, global mobility, and multicultural collaboration.

name: USA Biolympiad
description: The USA Biolympiad (USABO) is the nation’s top biology competition for high school students, with multiple exam rounds leading to advanced training for top finalists. The top four students go on to represent the U.S. at the International Biology Olympiad, where the team has consistently earned medals.

name: Congressional App Challenge
description: The Congressional App Challenge is a nationwide competition where high school students design and build their own apps to showcase coding skills. Open to students in participating districts, it promotes STEM education and provides recognition for innovative projects.

name: FIRST Robotics Competition
description: The FIRST Robotics Competition is a team-based event where high school students design and build large robots to compete in game-style challenges. Beyond engineering, it includes teamwork, fundraising, and outreach, helping students develop technical and leadership skills while competing for awards and scholarships.

name: Conrad Challenge
description: The Conrad Challenge is a global competition where students ages 13–18 design innovative solutions to real-world problems while developing entrepreneurial skills. Teams progress through multiple stages and present their ideas at the Innovation Summit, competing for scholarships and recognition.

name: Games for Change Student Challenge
description: The Games for Change Student Challenge is an annual competition where students create games and projects focused on social impact topics like sustainability and community improvement. Open to middle and high school students, it offers international recognition and prizes, including scholarships.

name: picoCTF Competition
description: picoCTF is a global cybersecurity competition where students solve challenges in hacking, cryptography, and reverse engineering to capture digital flags. Open to all skill levels, it helps participants build real-world cybersecurity and problem-solving skills.

name: National Cyber League (NCL) Competition
description: The National Cyber League (NCL) is a cybersecurity competition where students tackle real-world challenges like ethical hacking, forensics, and network security. Through individual and team games, participants build practical skills and receive a Scouting Report to showcase their strengths and career readiness.

name: Virginia Tech ICPC
description: The Virginia Tech ICPC program offers high school students the chance to compete in programming contests that build problem-solving and coding skills. It provides an accessible way for students interested in computer science to gain competitive programming experience.

name: National Cyber Cup by CYBER.org
description: The National Cyber Cup (NCC) is a free cybersecurity competition where students compete in capture-the-flag challenges to solve real-world security problems. Open to U.S. students in grades 4–12, it introduces participants to cybersecurity through team-based, hands-on experience.

name: DECA Inc.
description: DECA’s collegiate program helps students build leadership and career skills in areas like marketing, finance, and management. Through competitions, conferences, and real-world challenges, students gain experience and prepare for future careers in business.

name: Berkeley Business Academy for Youth - High School Entrepreneurship
description: The Berkeley Business Academy for Youth (B-BAY) Entrepreneurship program is a two-week summer program where high school students develop and pitch their own business ideas. Through lectures, projects, and team activities, students build business, communication, and presentation skills while earning a certificate of completion.

name: Babson Summer Study
description: Babson Summer Study is a 3+ week online program for high school juniors and seniors focused on entrepreneurship and solving real-world problems. Students complete coursework, build key leadership skills, and earn 4 college credits while developing an innovative, changemaker mindset.

name: Global Youth Entrepreneurship Challenge
description: https://entreplanet.org/GYEC/index.php

name: Genius Olympiad
description: The GENIUS Olympiad is an international competition where high school students create projects addressing environmental issues across fields like science, business, art, and coding. It provides a global platform for students to showcase innovative solutions and collaborate on sustainability challenges.

name: Diamond Challenge
description: https://diamondchallenge.org/

name: BUILDING-U High School Internship
description: The BUILDING-U High School Internship is a free, online program where students work on real-world projects across areas like coding, marketing, and business. Open globally, it offers flexible, hands-on experience and opportunities for self-directed growth.

name: Wharton Global High School Investment Competition
description: The Wharton Global High School Investment Competition is a free program where teams of students build and manage a virtual investment portfolio while developing financial strategies. Guided by an advisor, participants gain experience in investing, teamwork, and analysis, with top teams competing at a global finale.

name: NFTE World Series of Innovation
description: The NFTE World Series of Innovation is a global competition where students develop creative solutions to real-world challenges aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Participants build entrepreneurial and problem-solving skills while competing for recognition and cash prizes.

name: Blue Ocean Student Entrepreneur Competition
description: The NFTE World Series of Innovation is a global competition where students develop creative solutions to real-world challenges aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Participants build entrepreneurial and problem-solving skills while competing for recognition and cash prizes.

name: Stanford Math Tournament (SMT)
description: The Stanford Math Tournament (SMT) is a competitive math event for high school students, attracting participants from around the world. It offers challenging problems through both in-person and online formats, promoting advanced mathematical thinking and accessibility.

name: PROMYS - Program in Mathematics for Young Scientists
description: PROMYS is a rigorous six-week summer math program at Boston University for highly motivated high school students. It emphasizes deep, proof-based learning and creative problem-solving in a collaborative mathematical community, with financial aid available.

name: American Mathematics Competitions (AMC)
description: The American Mathematics Competitions (AMC) is a series of prestigious math contests that develop problem-solving and analytical skills for middle and high school students. Through exams like AMC 10/12 and AIME, students can advance to higher-level competitions and showcase their mathematical ability.

name: United States Physics Olympiad (USAPhO)
description: The Purple Comet! Math Meet is an annual team mathematics competition for middle and high school students. Since its inception in 2003, it has offered a platform for students to showcase their problem-solving skills in mathematics. The competition is conducted online, typically in April. Teams are supervised and can register at any time, with team registration already underway. The competition aims to provide problems in multiple languages, catering to a diverse group of students globally. It's a free event that encourages participation from students interested in mathematics.

name: Purple Comet Math Meet
description: The Purple Comet! Math Meet is a free, online team competition where middle and high school students solve challenging math problems. Open to students worldwide, it promotes collaboration and problem-solving in a global setting.

name: Wharton High School Data Science Competition
description: The Wharton High School Data Science Competition is a free global event where students analyze sports data to make predictions about a simulated hockey league. Teams build data analysis and modeling skills while competing for recognition and prizes.

name: MathWorks Math Modeling Challenge (M3 Challenge)
description: The MathWorks Math Modeling Challenge (M3 Challenge) is a free, online competition where high school students use mathematical modeling to solve real-world problems. Teams collaborate over a single weekend, competing for significant scholarship prizes and recognition.

name: Math Kangaroo International Competition in Mathematics
description: Math Kangaroo is an annual international math competition for students in grades 1–12, designed to promote creative problem-solving and a love for mathematics. With both online and in-person options, it offers students a chance to compete and earn recognition at state and national levels.

name: TeamsCode Virtual Programming Contests
description: TeamsCode is a free, virtual programming competition where high school students compete in teams to solve algorithmic problems. With novice and advanced divisions, it helps students build coding and problem-solving skills while competing for prizes.

name: Never Such Innocence
description: Never Such Innocence engages students aged 9–18 in reflecting on the impact of war and conflict through poetry, art, and music, encouraging creativity, critical thinking, and global awareness. Its annual competition provides a platform for young voices worldwide, fostering cultural dialogue and peacebuilding while appealing to students interested in literature, the arts, philosophy, political science, and psychology.

name: Congressional Essay Contest
description: The Congressional Essay Contest, organized by The National Society of The Colonial Dames of America, invites high school students aged 16+ to write essays on annually changing topics related to government and politics. Winners earn a scholarship to attend a Congressional Seminar in Washington, D.C., featuring a Mock Congress and immersive experiences in government and history.

name: GRC Social Impact Essay Competition
description: The GRC Social Impact Essay Competition invites high school students worldwide to propose solutions to global challenges through argumentative essays on topics like sustainability, global health, and technology for good. With opportunities for mentorship, internships, and publication, it is ideal for students interested in leadership, innovation, and social impact.

name: AFSA High School Essay Contest
description: The AFSA High School Essay Contest invites students in grades 9–12 to explore issues in foreign service and international relations through a 1,000–1,500 word MLA-formatted essay. With major prizes including a $2,500 award and an all-expense paid trip to Washington, D.C., it is ideal for students interested in global affairs, research, and writing.

name: John F. Kennedy Profile in Courage Essay Contest
description: The AFSA High School Essay Contest invites students in grades 9–12 to explore issues in foreign service and international relations through a 1,000–1,500 word MLA-formatted essay. With major prizes including a $2,500 award and an all-expense paid trip to Washington, D.C., it is ideal for students interested in global affairs, research, and writing.
link: The John F. Kennedy Profile in Courage Essay Contest invites high school students to analyze an act of political courage by a U.S. elected official through a compelling essay. With top prizes up to $10,000, it is a prestigious opportunity for students interested in history, leadership, and political analysis.

name: Expanding Horizons Institute (EHI)
description: The Expanding Horizons Institute (EHI) supports first-generation, college-bound high school sophomores and juniors through seminars and paid summer internships focused on academic and career readiness. With SAT prep, networking, and college guidance, it is ideal for students seeking support in navigating higher education and professional pathways.

name: U.S. Department of the Interior Internship Program
description: The U.S. Department of the Interior Internship Program offers paid opportunities for students to gain hands-on experience in federal agencies while exploring career paths related to their studies. With flexible part-time or full-time roles, it provides a strong pathway into public service and potential future employment in the civil service.

name: United Nations Competitions and Contests
description: United Nations Competitions and Contests provide students with creative opportunities to engage with global issues like sustainability, social justice, and international development through formats such as essays, art, and media. Open to a wide range of ages, they are ideal for students looking to build creativity, critical thinking, and global awareness.

name: DoSomething.org
description: DoSomething.org empowers high school students to take action on social issues through free, year-round campaigns focused on areas like environmental conservation and civic engagement. It is ideal for students seeking flexible opportunities to make a meaningful impact while building leadership and activism skills.

name: U.S. Secret Service Student Volunteer Service Program
description: The U.S. Secret Service Student Volunteer Service Program offers high school and college students hands-on experience in a premier federal law enforcement agency through an academic-related, unpaid internship. With a commitment of at least 12 hours per week, it is ideal for students interested in public administration, political science, and law.

name: United States Earth Science Organization (USESO) Programs
description: The United States Earth Science Organization (USESO) offers programs like the National Open Exam, Training Camp, and LEES to prepare students for advanced study and competition in Earth science and environmental policy. It is ideal for students interested in environmental science, research, and global challenges related to sustainability.

name: JQA International Environmental Children's Drawing Contest
description: The JQA International Environmental Children’s Drawing Contest invites students worldwide to express their perspectives on environmental issues through creative artwork. It is an excellent opportunity for students to showcase their creativity while promoting environmental awareness and global consciousness.

name: NCF-Envirothon
description: NCF-Envirothon is a leading environmental competition that engages high school students in hands-on challenges across topics like ecology, forestry, soils, wildlife, and current environmental issues. With international participation and a strong focus on problem-solving and sustainability, it is ideal for students interested in environmental science and STEM.

name: Cooper Hewitt National High School Design Competition
description: The Cooper Hewitt National High School Design Competition challenges students to create innovative solutions to real-world problems inspired by design themes each year. It is ideal for students interested in creativity, problem-solving, and applying design thinking to make a meaningful impact.

name: EPA Challenges & Prizes
description: The EPA Challenges & Prizes initiative invites participants to solve environmental and public health issues through innovative competitions in areas like technology, research, and design. With substantial awards and diverse challenge topics, it is ideal for students interested in sustainability, innovation, and real-world problem solving.

name: NOAA Ocean Guardian Youth Ambassador Program
description: The NOAA Ocean Guardian Youth Ambassador Program empowers students ages 13–18 to lead conservation projects and engage in ocean stewardship through webinars, outreach, and collaboration. It is ideal for students interested in marine science, environmental advocacy, and leadership.

name: Science without Borders® Challenge – International Student Art Contest
description: The Science without Borders® Challenge invites students ages 11–19 to create artwork promoting ocean conservation and awareness of marine ecosystems. With scholarships and global recognition, it is ideal for students interested in art, environmental science, and advocacy.

name: Global Canvas Children's Art Competition
description: The Global Canvas Children’s Art Competition invites young artists aged 16 and under to create artwork centered on environmental and wildlife conservation themes. With creative freedom and meaningful prizes, it is ideal for students interested in art, sustainability, and raising awareness about endangered species.

name: Junior Science and Humanities Symposium
description: The Junior Science and Humanities Symposium (JSHS) is a prestigious STEM competition where high school students conduct and present original research across fields like engineering, computer science, and biology. With scholarship opportunities and a professional symposium experience, it is ideal for students interested in advanced research and STEM careers.

name: National Ocean Sciences Bowl
description: The National Ocean Sciences Bowl (NOSB) is an academic competition that engages high school students in ocean science through regional events focused on marine biology, oceanography, and environmental science. It is ideal for students interested in STEM careers related to oceans and environmental stewardship.

name: Environmentor - RISE
description: Environmentor, offered by RISE, is a summer research mentorship program where high school students conduct environmental studies on Jamaica Bay and the Rockaway shoreline alongside professional scientists. With hands-on fieldwork, skill training, and a stipend, it is ideal for students interested in environmental science and marine research.

name: The New York Times Student Contests
description: The New York Times Learning Network offers student contests that encourage creative engagement with current events through writing, multimedia, and visual storytelling. Open to students worldwide, they are ideal for those looking to build critical thinking skills and develop a strong, authentic voice.

name: International Photography Awards (IPA)
description: The International Photography Awards (IPA) is a global competition that recognizes photographers across professional, amateur, and student categories. With major prizes, exhibitions, and industry recognition, it is ideal for students looking to showcase their work and gain exposure in photography.

name: Scholastic Art and Writing Awards
description: The Scholastic Art and Writing Awards is a prestigious national program that recognizes student creativity in art and writing through scholarships, exhibitions, and awards. It is ideal for students looking to gain recognition, develop their talents, and showcase their creative work on a national level.

name: USAAAO
description: The USA Astronomy and Astrophysics Organization (USAAAO) promotes interest in astronomy through training resources and competitive exams that lead to selection for the International Olympiad for Astronomy and Astrophysics (IOAA). The program runs from January registration to February testing and concludes with the IOAA in August, with a $30 fee and available financial aid. Open to U.S. citizens and permanent residents, it aims to broaden access to astrophysics education.

name: Celebrating Art Contest
description: Celebrating Art is a nationwide contest for K–12 students that offers a chance to showcase artwork, gain recognition, and win prizes, including publication opportunities. Held three times a year, it also rewards teachers with art supplies and books through its partnership with Blick Art Materials. The program supports both student creativity and the growth of school art programs.

name: Design-A-Bag Competition
description: The Design-A-Bag (DAB) Competition is a global contest for design students and freelance designers to showcase creative bag designs based on an annual theme. Participants can win prizes such as cash, international trips, design courses, and media exposure. The competition fosters creativity and encourages a worldwide exchange of design ideas.

name: Leonard L. Milberg ’53 High School Poetry Prize
description: The Leonard L. Milberg ’53 High School Poetry Prize, hosted by Princeton University’s Lewis Center for the Arts, is a prestigious contest for 11th-grade students worldwide. Judged by Princeton’s creative writing faculty, it awards cash prizes up to $1,500 for outstanding poetry submissions. The competition provides a strong platform for young poets to gain recognition and showcase their work.

name: Congressional Art Competition
description: The Congressional Art Competition is a nationwide contest held each spring to recognize high school artists across every congressional district. Students submit work through their representative’s office, and winners are honored locally and in Washington, DC, with their art displayed in the U.S. Capitol for a year. With over 650,000 participants since 1982, it offers a highly prestigious platform for young artists.

name: Earplay Donald Aird Composers Competition
description: The Earplay Donald Aird Composers Competition is an annual global contest open to composers of all ages, honoring the legacy of Donald Aird. Participants submit original works for small ensembles, and the winner receives a $1,000 prize and a live performance by Earplay. The competition celebrates innovation in contemporary music, with results announced in the fall.

name: Reflection Arts Program - National PTA
description: The National PTA’s Reflections Arts Program invites students from Pre-K through grade 12 to create original artwork based on an annual theme, fostering creativity and self-expression. It includes multiple categories like dance, film, literature, music, photography, and visual arts, along with a division for students with disabilities. The program promotes artistic growth, confidence, and broader success in both the arts and life.

name: Doodle for Goodle
description: Doodle for Google is an annual contest where students design their own Google homepage doodle, showcasing creativity and artistic expression. Winners can receive prizes such as scholarships and technology grants, with details and themes changing each year. The competition offers a valuable platform for students interested in art, design, and digital creativity.

name: National Cyber Cup by CYBER.ORG
description: The National Cyber Cup (NCC) by CYBER.ORG is a free, jeopardy-style Capture the Flag competition for U.S. students in grades 4–12, with separate divisions for middle and high school. Designed to introduce cybersecurity, it gives participants hands-on experience with real-world challenges faced by professionals. Teams must register through an adult coach, with parental consent required.
